payload.title: Jamninkaornis
payload.wikitext:
{{Short description|Genus of extinct bird}} {{Speciesbox | fossil_range =
[[Late Oligocene]] (Chattian), ~{{fossilrange|26}} | image = Jamninkaornis kencampbelli (holotype, MSMD Av JAM2 1a+b).png | image_caption = Holotype specimen | display_parents = 2 | genus = Jamninkaornis | parent_authority = Bochenski et al., [[2026 in archosaur paleontology|2026]] | species = kencampbelli | authority = Bochenski et al., 2026 }} '''''Jamninkaornis''''' ({{lit|Jamninka bird}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of [[passerine]] bird in the suborder [[Tyranni]] (suboscines), known from the late [[Oligocene]] ([[Chattian]] age, {{Ma|26}}) of Poland. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Jamninkaornis kencampbelli''''', known from a single [[coracoid]] and [[humerus]] (pectoral and forelimb bones). == Discovery and naming == [[File:Oligocene bird fossil sites (Carpathian Arc).png|thumb|left|[[Type locality (biology)|Type locality]] in the [[Carpathian Mountains|Carpathian arc]] (Jamna Dolna: 9–10)]] The ''Jamninkaornis'' fossil material was discovered in rock outcrops near the former village site of [[Jamna Dolna]] in [[Podkarpackie Voivodeship]] (Subcarpathian province), southeast Poland. The specimen is housed at the Institute of Systematics and Evolution of Animals in [[Kraków]], where it is permanently [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as specimen MSMD Av JAM2_1a+b. It consists of a right [[coracoid]] ([[pectoral girdle]] bone) and [[humerus]] (upper forelimb bone), preserved on two separate slabs of rock. In 2026, Zbigniew M. Bochenski and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Jamninkaornis kencampbelli'' as a new genus and species of passerine bird based on these fossil remains, establishing MSMD Av JAM2_1a+b as the [[holotype]] specimen. The [[Genus|generic name]], ''Jamninkaornis'', combines a reference to [[:pl:Jamninka|Jamninka]], a stream and valley close to the [[Type locality (biology)|type locality]], with the [[Greek language|Greek]] word {{lang|grc|[[:wikt:ὄρνῑς|ὄρνῑς]]}} ({{lang|grc|órnīs}}), meaning {{gloss|bird}}. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''kencampbelli'', honors the American paleornithologist Kenneth E. Campbell Jr., and his research on fossil birds. {{gallery| |Jamninkaornis, comparison with extant suboscines.png|Coracoids (top) and humeri (bottom) of extant suboscines, compared to the corresponding elements in ''J. kencampbelli'' (far left, with interpretive drawing) }} == See also == * ''[[Crosnoornis]]'' and ''[[Wieslochia]]'', two other fossil suboscines == References == {{Reflist|refs= {{Cite journal |last1=Bochenski |first1=Zbigniew M. |last2=Tomek |first2=Teresa |last3=Szybiak |first3=Robert |last4=Wertz |first4=Krysztof |date=June 2026 |title=A new passerine (Aves: Passeriformes) and three other specimens of Late Oligocene birds from Poland, with a review of all Paleogene birds from the northern part of the Carpathian Arc |url=https://palaeo-electronica.org/content/2026/5902-late-oligocene-birds-from-poland |journal=[[Palaeontologia Electronica]] |volume=29 |issue=2 |article-number=29.2.a26 |doi=10.26879/1712 |doi-access=free}} }} {{Passeriformes|P.|state=autocollapse}} {{Taxonbar|from1=Q140310744|from2=Q140310745}} [[Category:Tyranni]] [[Category:Oligocene birds]] [[Category:Prehistoric birds of Europe]] [[Category:Chattian genera]] [[Category:Fossils of Poland]] [[Category:Monotypic prehistoric bird genera]] [[Category:Fossil taxa described in 2026]]
